- Human annotators rated summaries on factual consistency (categorizing errors), informativeness (using 1-5 stars for main points), and coherence (using 1-5 stars for structure and flow), with explanations required for imperfect ratings.

Annotators rate summaries on factual consistency (no error, minor error, major error), informativeness (1–5 stars from very poor to very good), and coherence (1–5 stars). Detailed star definitions and required explanations are provided in the annotation guidelines.

We also conducted a human annotation, focused on three aspects: (i) factual consistency where the summary has no factual errors and all the details in the summary are supported by the article, (ii) informativeness where the summary express the main points of the article and the summary content is important and relevant, and (iii) coherence where the summary has good structure and flow, is easy to follow, and facts in the summary are presented in logical order.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple guideline descriptions into one comprehensive statement. Normalized criteria capitalization. The human evaluation methodology is well-documented in the paper with detailed rating scales and annotation procedures.

overall_notes: The paper presents a high-quality dataset (CCSum) for abstractive news summarization. The extraction was generally accurate but required normalization of metric names and dataset references. The paper extensively evaluates summarization models using both automatic metrics and human evaluation, but does not use LLM-as-judge methodology. All human evaluation criteria and automatic metrics are clearly documented in the paper.
